rationale.palette: Light theme, as measured (16.3 light vs 0 dark) and as the world is: a whiteboard. Every role is a token from source/handout/handout.css [E7]: bg #FAFAF7 (--paper, also <meta theme-color> [E4] and the page background [E10]; 'never pure #FFF on a projector'), ink #1E2024 (--ink, black marker), ink2 #5C6068 (--ink-soft). CHANGED the accent order: the draft ranked blue first by area share (blue 19 % vs orange 9 %), but the material assigns jobs, not areas: 'orange → the ONE thing: stars, underlines, circles' and 'blue → structure. Blue never carries content' [E1, E2], and its own role token --highlight resolves to orange [E7]. So accent #EE6316 (--marker-orange, 3.1:1: fills, stars, big words only), accent2 #1F5BC4 (--marker-blue, 6.0:1), accent3 and ok #25874A (--dot-green, the dot-vote stickers), deny #D23A2F (--dot-red, replacing the draft's derived #D2444E), accentInk #B84A0C (--marker-orange-text, 5.0:1: orange words at text size), onAccent #1E2024 (5.0:1 on orange; white is 3.3:1). muted #686C74 is ink2's cool grey one step lighter (5.0:1; the draft's derived #737374 was warm-neutral), line #DADDE2 (--ghost: 'the ghost that stays behind is fine' [E2]). bg2 #EEEFEC is authored (one step darker paper for the board edge and tray; the draft's #EDEEF7 leaned toward the blue accent). warn #A97F00 is derived (the material has no warn colour; 3.5:1). Extra keys name the kit for the code: markerBlack/markerBlue/markerOrange, dotGreen/dotRed, ghost, and boardFrame #AEB4BC (authored aluminium edge of 'the big board' [E1]). paletteAlt removed: a whiteboard has no night stage and no scene is dark.
rationale.type: The material's own two voices [E5, E6, E8, E9, E23, E24]: Shantell Sans (--font-marker, OFL, a marker handwriting variable font) for display and body, and Caveat (--font-pen, OFL) for margin notes, stored as the extra role fonts.pen (the engine roles have no handwriting slot; the project module reads it). CHANGED fallbacks: the extractor filed Shantell Sans under grotesk (it is not in its handwriting list) and fell back to Helvetica Neue/Arial; the stacks now follow the material's own CSS (Comic Neue, Patrick Hand, cursive). serif, mono and cjk are unused system stacks (no copy needs them; the draft's JetBrains Mono and Source Serif 4 were generic defaults, not evidence). displayWeight 800 (the handout's h1 [E12]), bodyWeight 500; scale 20-168 px for board lettering (titles 108-136, boxed phrases 52-64, pen notes 40-52); tracking -0.01 em like the handout title, labels +0.04 em (caps tags such as BOX IT).
rationale.motion: Medium pace at 104 BPM: the notes are energetic in voice ('!!', arrows, ALL-CAPS ONE [E1, E2]) but the method is about clarity ('speed > beauty', 'one idea per box'), so things are written at marker speed and then stay readable. The draft's energy 0.61 is right; its data axis 0.76 is not: 86 digit tokens are lesson-plan clock times (20), minute durations (11), session-table cells (16) and counts like '3 markers' (39), plus 2 schedule tables and the handout's vector doodles counted as PDF figures [E19, E21]. CHANGED: dataViz false, HUD off, impact and whip dropped. Spring f 2.6 z 0.55 and overshoot 1.2 with outBack: the notes literally say 'corners can overshoot. Overshoot = alive.' [E2]. Transitions: match and cut only. The reel is one big board ('the big board stays up all session ... at the end we step back and look at the whole thing' [E1]; 'the zones are joined by big blue arrows, left → right' [E2]), so scene changes are camera flights along the board that follow a drawn blue arrow, and an eraser wipe ('short zig-zags, never circles' [E2]), all drawn inside the scenes; the compositor only cuts. typeReveal typing = the sequential write-on family: every word is written stroke by stroke with the marker (modules/ink.js), never blurred in.
rationale.sound: 104 BPM, G major (orange maps to G in the extractor's Scriabin table; G also suits ukulele-like plucks), light drums, organic SFX (paper, felt and marker, not glass). The workshop is hand-made and friendly, with a squeaky marker as its sound ('squeak = good marker' [E2]): the target is playful pizzicato and ukulele-like plucks with marker squeaks, cap pops and eraser swipes. The draft's bright-pop at 119 BPM with glassy SFX is the pastel product grammar (glassy is for cosmetics and glossy 3D) and its 119 BPM would rush the handwriting. audio/synth.py has no pizzicato, ukulele or squeak yet (stage 2 extends it): until then preset corporate is the nearest family that plays at 104 BPM (plucked motion, light kit), with instruments strings, pluck, marimba, bass, rim, shaker, kick. At 104 BPM a bar is 2.308 s: 13 bars = 30.0 s exactly and the short cut is 6 bars = 13.85 s.
rationale.narration: Off, as drafted, but for the right reasons: a music-led teaser for a workshop, 14 s and 30 s, likely muted autoplay, and every idea is on the board as handwriting. The draft's reason ('data 0.76') was a false positive. If a cut is narrated: Achird (friendly) with [warm, friendly], en-US, the facilitator's conversational register (second person, short lines [E1]).
rationale.visuals: vector only: the whiteboard, the marker ink and every prop (three markers, the felt eraser) are drawn in code, because the material's world is a board you draw on. CHANGED from vector, app-ui, pdf-figures, web-shots: the handout is a print-out, not an app, and its doodles are redrawn live on the board instead of shown as a PDF figure. No characters (no mascot in the material), no data viz (no data).
